title: introduce-synthetic-tool-manifest-and-indexed-event-framing-for-openai-compat
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: OpenAI-compat tool/function calling encounters ambiguous schema mappings when models emit tool names that differ from registered runtime tool IDs, and streaming fragments can be dropped or interleaved which causes tool invocation reassembly failures. Existing compatibility layers either rely on exact schema matching or brittle fragment coalescing heuristics.

Summary: This PR adds a runtime-side "synthetic tool manifest" that materializes a normalized view of available tools at request time by merging model-declared tool descriptors with server-registered tool adapters. The manifest provides stable canonical IDs, property-level normalization rules, and soft aliases for name collisions. In parallel, the PR introduces an "indexed event framing" convention for the streaming path: each stream chunk related to tool selection/invocation carries a compact index header (xi=<sequence>) and tool token (ti=<canonical-id>) plus optional fragment metadata (frag=1/3). Clients can reassemble fragments deterministically using sequence indexes and tolerate lossy delivery with tombstone semantics.

Design highlights: 1) Synthetic manifest builder: merges model tool schema, runtime adapter schema, and openai-compat translation rules. Normalizers include type coercions (e.g. integer/string), enum mapping tables, and optional property renames. A collision resolution policy favors customer-registered adapters, then name-based heuristics, then model-declared canonical names; conflicts are surfaced as telemetry rather than hard errors. 2) Canonical tool IDs: runtime assigns stable short ids (e.g. t_7f3a) persisted for the request lifetime and referenced by stream headers to avoid repeated verbose schemas in streaming chunks. 3) Indexed event framing: SSE chunks include meta headers (xi, ti, frag, eof) emitted by the compatibility layer; downstream consumers (SDKs/clients) use xi to order fragments and to detect missing indexes; recovery rules include immediate fallback to non-streamed tool payloads and a best-effort continuation with model fallback. 4) Backwards compatibility: when talking to older clients or when upstream model only uses v1 envelopes, we fall back to the existing framed payload but still generate the synthetic manifest server-side for schema mapping. A feature flag (compat.synthetic_manifest=true) gates the rollout.

Testing & validation: unit tests for manifest merging, collision resolution, and canonical id generation; integration harness that simulates fragmented streams, dropped chunks, and out-of-order delivery to validate reassembly and tombstone behavior; end-to-end smoke test against the openai-compat adapter and Redwood SDK (python & ts) stubs.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag for 2 weeks in canary, collect telemetry counters (manifest_collision, fragment_recovery_rate, tool_mismatch_fallback), then enable for 20% production traffic, monitor for increased bad-invoke rates, and then full rollout.

Why this is different: instead of only normalizing schema names or improving fragment stitching heuristics, this approach creates a transient, authoritative manifest per request and a compact, index-based streaming envelope that makes reassembly deterministic and debuggable while preserving OpenAI-compat semantics for tool_choice/tool_call scenarios.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Architecturally this looks sound. Two asks: (1) add an explicit TTL for synthetic canonical ids so we don't leak them across long-lived connections, and (2) show an example of the SSE chunk with xi/ti headers in the docs.

Priya Kapoor (author): Added ttl config to manifest builder (default 2 minutes) and expanded docs with a streaming example. See packages/openai-compat/src/manifest/builder.ts and docs/openai-compat/synthetic-manifest.md

Sofia Chen: Unit tests look good; can you add a collision-case test where model and runtime both declare the same tool but with incompatible param types? We should assert telemetry is emitted and the request falls back gracefully.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added manifest.collision.test.ts to cover incompatible types; telemetry emitted as "manifest_collision" with tags {tool, request_id}.
Marta Ivanov: CI failed initially on the lint step for naming in framing.ts. Once fixed, re-run CI and ensure the python SDK adapter is exercised in the matrix job before merging.
Priya Kapoor (author): Fixed lint, updated matrix job to include sdk/python. All CI checks passed on rerun.
release_notes: Introduce synthetic tool manifest + indexed event streaming framing to improve tool/function-call compatibility and deterministic fragment reassembly. Feature flagged; rollout plan included.

squash: introduce synthetic manifest and indexed framing

Summary of changes: created manifest builder, stream framing encoder/decoder, SDK adapters, tests and docs.
notes: Feature gated (compat.synthetic_manifest). Monitor telemetry after canary. SDKs updated to interpret xi/ti headers; older clients continue to receive legacy envelopes.
